    Security

    How your messages are protected

    Every message is encrypted on your phone before it is sent. It can only be decrypted with two keys together:

    Base key in the invite (QR code) · never sent to the server
    +
    Epoch key new with every member change and once a day
    Room key of the epoch encrypts and decrypts the messages

    How a new epoch key reaches every member

    1. Alice makes a new epoch key e.g. because Dave joins — random, only on her phone
    2. One envelope per member she locks a copy with the public key of each member — only the private key on that member's phone opens it
      Alice Bob Dave Eve (removed)
    3. Signed and packed she signs the envelopes and the member list with her key and wraps everything with the base key
    4. The server only passes it on it stores the locked package for members who are offline — it can open none of the envelopes
    5. Every phone opens its own envelope Bob checks Alice's signature and opens his envelope with his private key. Eve got no envelope — she can not read on.

    How a message is sent

    Text signed room key server members
    • Base key — created with the room and only passed on in the invite: the QR code or the copied code of "Share". It never goes to the server, so the server can never read your messages.
    • Epoch key — every time a member joins, leaves or is removed (and once a day) a new one is made. Each member gets it in its own envelope that only its device can open. Whoever left or was removed gets no new key and can not read on.
    • Only both together open a message. The server stores the envelopes but can not open them — each one is sealed for the device of one member (and wrapped with the base key). Someone with an old invite has the base key but no epoch key.
    • Join code (TOTP) — even the encrypted messages only go to members: every time the app connects, it proves membership with a one-time code from the join secret of the current epoch (valid once, for a few minutes). The join secret changes with every epoch, so a removed member can not even fetch the encrypted messages anymore. The server knows the join secret to check the codes — it opens no message.
    • Signed — every message is signed by its sender (). Messages with a wrong signature are never shown, nobody can write in someone else's name.

    Please take care

    • Share invites in person. The invite contains the base key. Whoever gets the QR code or the copied code can ask to join — a photo of the QR code too.
    • "Copy Code" over another messenger gives the base key to that service. A PIN helps only a little.
    • Only accept requests you expect and compare the fingerprint on both phones before you accept.
    • Check the members now and then. Remove devices you do not know or that were lost.

    What the server sees

    Sees
    • Room ids and times
    • Which device is in which room
    • Approximate size (padded)
    • The join secret (to check join codes — it decrypts nothing)
    Never sees
    • Messages, images, files
    • Names, room name, member list
    • Base key and epoch keys (envelopes only sealed)

      Edit Room

      Fill the form to update the Chat Room

      • Push Notifications
      • You get a notification when a new message arrives while the app is closed. It never shows the content or the sender.
      • Keep on Server
      • Your messages and files are kept encrypted on the server until their lifetime ends, so members who are offline still get them later. When off, only members who are online right now receive them. It is set when the room is created and can not be changed.
      • Max. lifetime
      • Messages in this room are deleted after this time at the latest. It is set when the room is created and can not be changed.
      • Delete after
      • Your own messages are deleted after this time — earlier than the room allows, if you like. Only fixed steps are offered — an individual time would make your messages recognizable to the server.
